analyst_view.overall: Arouca (5th, 20 points, only 8 conceded in 11 games) host Rio Ave (17th, 7 points, 24 conceded, no league win since 11 October) on matchday 12. The match has an extra storyline: Rio Ave coach Vasco Seabra left Arouca for Rio Ave on 4 October when Rio Ave paid his release clause, and returns to face his old side, now coached by Vítor Severino (4 wins in 6). Both teams went out of the Taça de Portugal last week (Arouca 1-2 at Mafra, Rio Ave 0-1 at Vianense), so neither has extra fixtures to worry about. Arouca had Pedro Santos and Puche injured before the Mafra game with no update on their fitness, while Rio Ave get Celso Aguilera (back from a cruciate ligament injury) and Nelson Abbey back in the squad; the numbers list no absences for either side. No referee has been named yet, and news is fairly thin, so the view stays close to the numbers with a small trim on Arouca's attack.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, with Arouca at 1.8 against a Rio Ave defence that has let in 13 in its last six (already counted). I trim slightly to about 2.7 because Arouca's Pedro Santos and Puche were injured before the cup game at Mafra and there is no word that they are back, which the numbers don't know; it is a small move since their status is unclear and Rio Ave's leaky defence still points to goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 5.6 to 4.1 for Arouca, already lifting Arouca a little because Rio Ave have conceded 36 corners in their last six. Rio Ave chasing points away from home under a coach who knows Arouca well could give them a bit more of the ball, but Arouca at home should still push most of the play; nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already trimming Arouca because Rio Ave have drawn few fouls lately and adding a little for Rio Ave's recent booking rate. Rio Ave are fighting relegation and Seabra's return to his old club adds some edge, but there is no history of bad blood and no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.6 shots and already take about 14% off Rio Ave, who managed only 51 shots in their last six, and add about 7% to Arouca against a Rio Ave side that has allowed 93. Arouca's possible absences point slightly down, but Rio Ave needing a result could open the game up, so these pull both ways and I stay at 23.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target, with small form changes already in. I go a touch lower, to about 8.2, for the same reason as goals: Arouca may still be without the injured Pedro Santos and Puche, which the numbers can't see, while Rio Ave's attack (no league win since mid-October) gives little reason to push it up.
